description: Renovate configuration for mcp-plugins (Python server, pinned MCP servers, CI)

npm.description: The third-party MCP servers: exact versions in package.json, the whole tree in package-lock.json

customManagers.description: Claude Code version the CI lint:plugin job validates the manifests with

packageRules.description: Everything the plugin locks soaks 14 days. For Python this matches [tool.uv] exclude-newer = "14 days", which also holds back transitive packages in lock-file maintenance; a direct pin newer than that would not resolve. npm has no such window: its transitive packages get only the audit:deps scan.

Claude Code (CI lint:plugin, a customManager in .gitlab-ci.yml) soaks like the plugin's own dependencies; the MCP servers and mcp are already covered by the pep621/npm rule above. It releases several times a week, so it comes on the Monday run only.

Patch and minor updates of what the plugin locks automerge after the 14-day soak: test:python and lint:plugin run on the MR, and a merge reaches no installed copy until a person cuts a plugin release. Major stays a manual merge.

One Python version in two places: plugins/homelab/server/.python-version (what uv runs locally and in the plugin) and the -python3.X suffix of the CI uv image. Renovate keeps an image tag's suffix, so it cannot move them together; a lone .python-version bump would leave test:python without its interpreter. Upgrade Python by hand in both.

The CI uv image soaks like the dependencies it locks. GHCR publishes no release dates, so the soak cannot be checked and timestamp-optional lets the MR open (with timestamp-required Renovate would create no branch and only list it on the Dependency Dashboard). test:python runs inside this image on the MR.
